summary: Fixed the capacity 'Run Calibration -> internal server error' (and any object-detection) failure that appeared as 'persistent detector write failed: write |1: The pipe has been ended' with the request dying in ~100ms. Root cause: the persistent YOLO detector and the training runner spawned their Python child with cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr. When the app runs without a valid console — a relaunched/detached/Windows-service process, i.e. exactly the state after restarting the app to apply a restore — os.Stderr is an invalid handle, and inheriting it makes Python fail its stdio initialization and exit immediately, before it can read the first frame. The detector then hits a broken stdin pipe on its next write. Both spawns now redirect the child's stderr through a Go-created pipe drained to the app log, which is always valid regardless of the parent's console state and also surfaces the worker's ready/traceback lines in the structured log for diagnosis. Verified by running the real CUDA yolo worker end-to-end. Confirmed the earlier CREATE_NO_WINDOW change was not the cause.
compatibility: No API/config change. The detector/trainer worker's stderr now goes to the application log (prefixed 'vision detector:' / 'training:') instead of the console; stdout handling (the JSON protocol) is unchanged. Cross-platform (the os.Stderr inheritance was fragile on any OS without a controlling terminal).
